title: Monorepo skeleton with pnpm workspaces, Turborepo and Go modules
description: Stand up the polyglot monorepo described in ADR-0001 so that TypeScript and Go builds coexist with independent, cacheable pipelines.
acceptance: pnpm install succeeds from a clean clone with no manual steps
turbo run build succeeds across all TypeScript packages
go build ./... succeeds for every service under services/
Shared tsconfig.base.json is extended by every TypeScript package rather than duplicated
Turborepo remote caching is configured and documented, even if disabled by default

tests.desc: Clean-clone CI job runs install and build with no cached state and succeeds
Workspace manifest lints — every package has name, version and the required scripts
A second developer follows README setup on a clean machine and reaches a running build

title: CI pipelines: lint, typecheck, test, Go test, path filtering
description: GitHub Actions workflows gating every pull request. Go and TypeScript run in parallel and are independently gated. Path filters keep unrelated changes from running the whole matrix.
acceptance: Separate workflows for TypeScript and Go, running concurrently
Jobs gate on real exit codes — no piping test output to tail or grep
Path filtering: a docs-only change does not run the Go test matrix
Pipeline completes in under 8 minutes on a warm cache
Required status checks are configured on the main branch

tests.desc: A PR with a deliberately failing TypeScript test is blocked from merging
A PR with a deliberately failing Go test is blocked from merging
A docs-only PR completes without triggering the Go matrix

title: Local development stack via Docker Compose
description: One command brings up ClickHouse, Postgres, Redpanda, Redis and MinIO with health checks, seeded schemas and no manual configuration.
acceptance: pnpm dev:stack brings every service to healthy within 90 seconds
Health checks gate dependent services so startup order is deterministic
Named volumes persist data across restarts; dev:stack:down removes them
Ports are documented and do not collide with common local defaults
Redpanda console and ClickHouse play UI are reachable for debugging

tests.desc: CI brings the stack up, asserts every health check passes, and tears it down
Restarting the stack preserves previously written data
Fresh machine with only Docker installed reaches a healthy stack

title: Control-plane schema in Postgres with Drizzle migrations
description: Tenants, users, memberships, connectors, cases, case transitions, actions, approvals and audit. Forward-only migrations with a documented rollback procedure per migration.
acceptance: Every tenant-scoped table carries a non-null tenant_id
Migrations run forward cleanly from an empty database
Each migration documents its rollback procedure, even if that is restore-from-backup
Seed script provisions two tenants with distinct data for isolation testing
Schema is documented in docs/architecture/data-model.md and regenerated, not hand-maintained

tests.desc: Migrations apply cleanly to an empty database in CI
Seed script is idempotent — running it twice leaves identical state
Schema lint asserts no tenant-scoped table is missing tenant_id

title: Postgres row-level security and the tenant context boundary
description: Implements ADR-0008. RLS forced on every tenant-scoped table; the application role cannot bypass it; tenant context is established once at the request edge and a repository cannot be constructed without it.
acceptance: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is enabled on every tenant-scoped table
The application database role lacks BYPASSRLS
Middleware sets app.tenant_id per transaction from the authenticated session
Constructing a repository outside a tenant context throws at construction time, not at query time
A CI check enumerates tenant-scoped tables and fails if any lacks a policy

tests.desc: Cross-tenant read returns zero rows for every tenant-scoped table
A query deliberately written without a tenant_id filter still returns only the current tenant's rows
Repository construction without tenant context throws
Adding a new tenant-scoped table without a policy fails the CI schema check

title: Hash-chained append-only audit log
description: Implements the audit half of ADR-0007. Each entry hashes its predecessor; the application role holds INSERT and SELECT only; a verifier detects any break in the chain.
acceptance: entry_hash = SHA256(prev_hash || canonical_json(row)) with a stable canonical JSON encoding
The application role has no UPDATE or DELETE grant on audit_log
actor_type distinguishes human, ai, system and connector
A verifier walks the chain for a tenant and reports the first break with its entry id
The verifier runs as a scheduled job and alerts on failure

tests.desc: Chain verifier accepts a well-formed chain of 1000 entries
Verifier detects a mutated payload and reports the correct entry id
Verifier detects a deleted middle entry
An UPDATE issued as the application role is rejected by Postgres grants
Canonical JSON encoding is stable across key insertion order

title: Design tokens package — the Control Room theme
description: Colour, typography, spacing, elevation and motion tokens per docs/design/ui-ux-spec.md. Dark-first with a light mode. The severity ramp must be distinguishable without colour.
acceptance: Tokens exported as CSS custom properties, a Tailwind v4 theme, and typed TypeScript constants from one source
Dark and light themes both defined; dark is the default
Every text/background pair in the palette meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast
Severity is encoded by hue, icon and label — never by hue alone
A contrast-checking test runs in CI over the generated token pairs

tests.desc: Automated contrast check asserts AA compliance for all defined foreground/background pairs
Severity tokens each carry a distinct icon and label, asserted programmatically
Deuteranopia and protanopia simulation review of the severity ramp

title: Shared UI component library on the design tokens
description: Base components built on Radix primitives and the token package: button, badge, severity pill, card, table, dialog, toast, empty state, skeleton. No hardcoded colour values anywhere.
acceptance: Every component consumes tokens; a lint rule rejects hardcoded hex values in packages/ui
All interactive components are keyboard operable and have visible focus states
Components render correctly in both themes
Each component has documented props and at least one usage example
Loading, empty and error states exist for every data-bearing component

tests.desc: Component render tests in both light and dark themes
Keyboard navigation test — tab order and focus visibility for every interactive component
axe accessibility assertions pass with no violations
Lint rule fails on an introduced hardcoded hex value

title: Authentication, sessions and role-based access control
description: Email and OAuth sign-in, secure session handling, and the role model: owner, admin, analyst, read-only, plus the MSP role that spans client tenants.
acceptance: Sessions are httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Lax with server-side revocation
Roles are enforced server-side on every endpoint; the UI only hides, never protects
The MSP role grants scoped access to explicitly linked client tenants and nothing else
Failed sign-ins are rate limited per account and per IP
Every authentication event is written to the audit log

tests.desc: Each role is denied every endpoint outside its permission set
An MSP user cannot read a tenant they are not linked to
Session revocation takes effect immediately on the next request
Brute-force attempt is rate limited and audited

title: Observability baseline — OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and structured logs
description: Tracing, metrics and structured logging wired into every service from the start, with trace context propagating across the Go and TypeScript boundary.
acceptance: trace_id propagates from an ingested event through to a delivered alert
Logs are structured JSON and always carry tenant_id and trace_id
No secret, credential or raw log payload is ever logged — enforced by a redaction layer
Golden-signal metrics are exported and visible in a local Grafana
A developer can answer 'why did this alert take 4 minutes' from a single trace

tests.desc: A synthetic event produces one unbroken trace spanning Go and TypeScript services
Redaction layer strips known secret patterns from log payloads
Every expected golden-signal metric is present after a synthetic run

title: Shared schema package with Go code generation
description: One definition of the OCSF event, Signal, Case and Action contracts, generating both TypeScript types and Go structs so the two planes cannot disagree.
acceptance: Contracts are defined once in packages/schema
Go structs are generated, not hand-written
CI regenerates and fails on any diff against committed output
Schema changes are versioned with an explicit compatibility policy
Generated code is clearly marked as generated and excluded from manual edits

tests.desc: CI regeneration produces no diff on an unchanged schema
Round-trip serialisation TypeScript to Go to TypeScript preserves every field
A breaking schema change without a version bump fails the compatibility check

title: Live project progress dashboard on GitHub Pages
description: A single page showing phase completion, ticket status, test-case coverage and burndown, rebuilt automatically by a GitHub Action whenever issues change.
acceptance: Published to GitHub Pages at a stable URL
Rebuilds automatically on issue open, close, label change and board move
Shows per-phase progress, ticket counts by status, and aggregate test-case counts
Degrades gracefully when the API is unavailable — serves the last good build
Renders correctly on a phone and in both colour schemes

tests.desc: Workflow builds and deploys successfully from a clean checkout
Generator produces correct counts from a fixture issue set
Page is legible at 375px width in light and dark mode
